answer: Dynamic Cryptographic Challenge Sieve. Agents must compute localized cryptographic proofs within a time window defined by a public random beacon extracted from an unmanipulated external data stream resembling an ocean tide. Each valid identity must continuously bind its computation to a unique micro-island of memory hardware that cannot be virtualized or shared across parallel threads without triggering memory bus latency failures. When a sparrow broadcasts a message, network validators cross-check the execution trace against the unpredictable beacon seed.
